transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... I just can't stop seeing this rough, sunken-looking patch on my face. Every time I look in the mirror, or if I see a photo of myself, it's just right there glaring at me. It makes one whole side of me look old and beat-up, even though my wife and people around me keep saying they barely notice anything. 

Like, speaking of photos, I'm a construction laborer, and we were actually taking some pictures the other day at this big site we just finished out by the highway. Man, that job was an absolute nightmare. The supply chain issues are still messing everything up, so we were waiting on these custom windows for like three months. My boss was losing his mind calling the distributor every single morning. He’s got this really loud voice, you can hear him yelling from the other side of the lot over the generators and everything. He’s a good guy though, just stressed out. We all are, really, especially with the cost of groceries and everything going up lately. My wife went to buy eggs the other day and couldn't believe it... 

But yeah, anyway, they showed me one of those group photos from the site, and I didn't even care about the house behind us. I just couldn't stop staring at that sunken patch on my cheek.
Does this concern about the appearance of that patch on your face cause you a lot of distress, or make it hard for you to do things you normally would, like socializing or taking pictures?

Yeah, it really does. I mean, it’s gotten to the point where I’ve been late getting out the door for the construction jobs in the mornings because I'm just stuck in the bathroom staring at it. Which is a real problem, because if you hit the highway even ten minutes late, you're stuck in that bumper-to-bumper mess by the new overpass they're building. I swear they've been working on that same stretch of road for two years. My buddy Mike drives a cement truck for that project, and he says the city inspectors are always holding things up with paperwork. 

But anyway, yeah, I've been dodging those site photos whenever the guys try to take them. Everyone’s got a smartphone now, you know? You can't even eat your lunch on a bucket without someone snapping a picture to put on the internet. The cameras on those things are so sharp now, they catch every single detail, which is exactly what I don't want. 

And it's not just at work, either. I've actually been skipping out on our family game nights lately. We usually play Yahtzee or cards, and my wife always makes those little cocktail wieners in the crockpot. They're really good, she puts brown sugar and barbecue sauce in there, gets the recipe from her sister down in Florida. But lately I just make an excuse and stay in the bedroom. I just... I really don't want people looking at my face. It just bothers me too much.
Outside of your concern about the patch on your face, have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still like doing stuff, you know? Like I said, I usually love those family game nights, and I still like working on my old Chevy in the garage on weekends. Well, when I can find the parts, anyway. Trying to find a good carburetor for a '78 C10 these days is like pulling teeth. I went to three different scrap yards last month, and the guys working there look at you like you're speaking Greek when you ask for anything older than a 2010. One guy, this kid who couldn't have been more than nineteen, tried to sell me a part for a Ford. A Ford! Can you believe that? I told him, "Son, you don't put Ford parts in a Chevy, that's just against the laws of nature." He just shrugged and went back to looking at his phone. Kids these days, I swear they don't know how to turn a wrench to save their lives. It's all computers and sensors now. If your check engine light comes on, you practically need an IT degree to figure out why. 

But yeah, I haven't been feeling hopeless or anything like that. I still enjoy my truck and watching the game on Sundays. It's just... I just don't want people staring at this spot on my cheek while I'm trying to do those things.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent preoccupation with an imagined or slight defect in appearance (specifically, a 'sunken patch' on the face), which causes significant distress and impairment in social and occupational functioning. There is no evidence of depressive symptoms or significant anxiety outside of appearance concerns, and no indication of delusional beliefs, which rules out major depressive disorder and body dysmorphic disorder with psychotic features. The preoccupation is not better explained by another mental disorder, supporting the diagnosis of Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD), ICD-10 code F45.22.
